title: nullroute hardening profile
description: A distribution-independent statement of what must be true of a built nullroute image. Every assertion carries an executable verifier that inspects the built artifact or the running device. Backends are advisory: a backend is correct when the unchanged verifiers pass against its output, not when someone reviewed its recipe.

tier.description: 0: reproducible signed image, nothing irreversible. 1: adds a dm-verity hash tree over the system partition and a boot-time attestation display. 2: adds a signed boot chain rooted in fused silicon, which is irreversible. A profile must not assert a capability above its declared tier.

boards.description: Board identifiers this profile targets. A tier 2 profile may list only boards whose silicon supports a verified boot chain.

backends.description: How to build this, per distribution. ADVISORY ONLY, and the verifier is forbidden from reading this key (INV-PROV-2). Recorded so that adding a second distribution is a matter of adding an entry rather than rewriting the tooling.

assertions.description: What must be true of the built artifact or the running device. This is the contract.

excluded_controls.description: Controls from a published baseline that are deliberately NOT applied, with the reason. Publishing this is worth more than a compliance percentage: roughly a third of a general-purpose server baseline is vacuous or actively wrong on an air-gapped single-application device, and a high score achieved by applying controls that do nothing would be misleading.

pin.description: Exact commit or tag. Pin the commit: rpi-image-gen removed INI config support in v2.8.0 and breaks between minor versions.

status.description: `supported` requires that the UNCHANGED verifier suite passes in CI against an artifact this backend produced. Nothing else earns the word.

id.description: Unique across the repository, reported alongside the code invariants.

statement.description: A falsifiable claim about the built artifact or the running device.

stage.description: WHERE the fact is observable. `image` reads the built artifact offline; `boot` reads the running device. An assertion answerable only on a running system must not claim `image`, because offline inspection of mount options and kernel parameters produces false passes: the checks pass vacuously when /proc is absent.

verify.description: Executable verifiers. At least one is mandatory (INV-PROV-1): an assertion with an intent and no verifier is unfalsifiable, and unfalsifiable hardening is the failure mode this whole design exists to avoid.

rationale.description: Why this matters on THIS device. A rationale that would read identically in a generic server baseline is a sign the control was imported rather than chosen.

does_not_cover.description: REQUIRED (INV-PROV-34). What this assertion does not establish. Forcing the honest wording at authoring time is cheaper than discovering an overclaim in the threat model later.

tier.description: Minimum tier at which this assertion applies. Defaults to the profile's tier.

standard.description: Control ids from a published baseline, e.g. ANSSI-BP-028 R11. Cited, not shipped as a scanner.

check.description: Verifier implementation under provisioning/checks/, keyed by this name.

params.description: Arguments to the verifier. Shape is the verifier's own concern.

tool.description: External tool this verifier shells out to, if any. Must appear in the profile's tool allowlist so the verification path's own dependencies are enumerable.

reason.description: Why the control does not apply here. 'Not applicable' alone is not a reason.
